newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek equities end 0.37pct up, construction leads.
newsitem.headline: Greek equities end 0.37pct up, construction leads.

text.p: Athens stocks settled 0.37 percent higher on low volume with construction shares leading the advance and analysts said they expected the market to consolidate by end-April.
"The market will stabilise through April. The general share index will fluctuate from 1,200 to 1,300 points," said analyst George Athanasakis at Alpha Securities.
Institutional and retail investors are restructuring their portfolios based on fundamentals considering current price level attractive, he said.
"Further easing inflation forecasts will lead to a new rise in the bourse in May. Investors are awaiting the outcome of company financial results and particularly dividends," he added.
This rise will be milder than the "exaggerated" January rally, he said.
"Investors' focus is now concentrated on market fundamentals," said Athanasakis.
The banking sector and medium capitalisation stocks will be the strong performers of bourse's rise, he added.
"Especially in the banking sector, the market is expecting news of mergers and acquisitions," he added.
Another analyst said the market's support level was at 1,250 points.

"The bourse's support level is at 1,250 points and its resistance at 1,290 points. If this resistance is broken, the new one will be set around 1,320 points," said George Kissandrakis, an analyst at Northern Greece Securities.
Construction shares, banking stocks and blue chips will be the leaders of this new rally, he said.
In the U.S., the Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans to 5.50 percent.
"The news did not seem to affect the Greek bourse on Wednesday. However, in the medium term investors in U.S. markets might shift to emerging markets, such as Greece," he added.

There have been strong rumours in the stock exchange about more fines on securities firms for violation of the bourse's legislative framework, especially with regard to the recent Delta Securities scandal, he said.
"However, the market expects the fines to be relatively low and it should not be adversely affected in the next two days," he added.

The Athens general share index ended 0.37 percent or 4.77 points higher at 1,280.00 points from Monday's 1,275.23 close after opening at 1278.99. Turnover was 9.0 billion drachmas on volume of 2.8 million shares.

Advancers led decliners 125 to 81 with 28 issues unchanged on 234 traded. Most sectoral indices ended slightly higher with construction and insurance shares leading the rise, gaining 1.11 percent and 0.70 percent respectively.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 982.00-1020.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, closed up 65 drachmas at 5,765.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $41.87-$43.56. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 1,470-1,646 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
